prompt: Complete StreamCounter.countBytes so it reads an InputStream one byte at a time with read() until end of stream and returns how many bytes it read.
explanation: InputStream.read() returns an int rather than a byte precisely so that every real byte value (0..255) can be told apart from the special end-of-stream marker -1. A byte 0xFF arrives as the int 255, never -1, so the loop keeps counting until the stream itself ends. The standard read loop -- while ((n = in.read()) != -1) -- is the foundation of nearly all byte-stream processing in Java.
hints: in.read() returns one byte at a time; -1 means the stream is finished.
Use a while loop whose condition calls in.read() and compares against -1.
Increment a counter inside the loop body and return it after the loop ends.
